correctness.rationale: A prescribed-size coloring induces the edge vector of a disjoint union of cliques of sizes r_a, uniformly relabeled. With B the unsigned incidence of K_N, BBᵀ=(N−2)I+J and the orthogonal pair modules are constants, Bᵀ of centered vertex vectors, and ker B, of dimensions 1, N−1 and N(N−3)/2. To check scalar action directly, covariance depends only on equal, incident or disjoint edge pairs; their matrices are spanned by I, BᵀB and the all-ones matrix. The total pair sum is deterministic. Each row of the co-color pair array has random degree r_color−1 with variance s², and the row covariance off diagonal is −s²/(N−1) because the sum of rows is fixed. Dividing the centered row eigenvalue by N−2 recovers the star eigenvalue. The pairwise variance p(1−p) fixes the trace and hence the cycle eigenvalue, including N=4. Centering degrees by 2W/N and using the incidence identity gives the stated star projection norm; subtracting both the constant and star norms gives the residual norm and hence the variance formula. For a binary additive edge vector a_i+a_j, unequal coefficients a_i>a_j differ by one, since comparison to any third vertex gives a positive difference of bits. All other coefficients then equal −a_j. As N≥4 their mutual bit is 0 or 1, giving a star or co-star; equal coefficients give a constant graph. Of those graphs only the empty, complete and co-star are unions of cliques. The star mode vanishes exactly when the clique degrees are all equal. The two null modes therefore yield exactly the four stated graph cases. In the one-singleton case the statistic is m−d_H(J) for a uniform singleton J, independently confirming the regular-graph condition. The frozen checks were inspected, not executed; N=4–8 checks range over histogram multisets, and for all graphs at N=4,5 the classifications are compared to the formula, with direct coloring tests for a subset of cases. They are finite corroboration, not a substitute for the proof.
residual_risks: The decomposition labels invariant subspaces; if eigenvalues coincide their dimensions must be added for the numerical multiplicity. The result is for unrestricted fixed-histogram assignments, not proper colorings or the law with only the number of blocks fixed.

evidence: Filmus–Ihringer Theorem 1.2 states that for k,N−k≥2 every Boolean degree-one function on J(N,k) is constant or depends on one coordinate. At k=2 the coordinate x_i of a subset is one exactly on the edges of the star centered at i. Thus the theorem gives empty, complete, star and co-star, exactly the frozen Step 4 binary lemma. The multiplicity-free pair modules also belong to the standard Johnson scheme; equal-block perfect hypermatchings are a narrower representation-theoretic application.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Johnson result covers the full auxiliary graph classification, not only its equal-size case. Applying it to both the tested graph and the fixed cluster template removes any need for a new binary classification.

evidence: Schur averaging for any deterministic edge template z gives Var⟨w,πz⟩=Σ_{α=1,2}||P_αw||²||P_αz||²/d_α. Indeed center z to remove constants; averaging its outer product over permutations commutes with the pair action, and its trace on module α is ||P_αz||². For the cluster graph these squared norms are Ns²/(N−2) and Mp(1−p)−Ns²/(N−2), from row degrees and binary entries. Thus the eigenvalues are the displayed norms divided by d_1=N−1 and d_2=N(N−3)/2, without any new pair-moment theorem. The first projection vanishes iff the graph is regular; by Theorem 1.2 the second vanishes iff the graph is empty, complete, a star or a co-star.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In each mode one factor must vanish. For the cluster template regularity is equality of sizes and the four-graph list loses only the star. Intersecting those two conditions gives all histogram exceptions and graph cases immediately. This is specialization of standard orthogonality and an exact earlier Boolean classification, not just a vague similarity of representations.

originality.rationale: No inspected catalogue hit states the full prescribed-size theorem verbatim. Nevertheless, both parts are mechanically covered: Schur orthogonality for the standard three pair modules gives the complete variance decomposition for an arbitrary uniformly relabeled edge vector, and the known classification of Boolean degree-one functions on J(N,2) gives exactly the binary additive graphs used to determine the null modes. Specialization to a disjoint union of cliques requires only its deterministic degree multiset and the fact that a star on N≥4 is not a union of cliques. The failure is by explicit mathematical implication, not by the inaccessible equal-block citation or by a near title match.
residual_risks: This is a statement-level implication, not a claim that an earlier paper prints the same all-histogram formulas or proves historical priority. Exact coverage of the unavailable cited equal-block source remains unresolved.

value.rationale: A zero-variance diagnostic for fixed-histogram permutation tests is naturally motivated and the presentation is useful. The exact diagnostic in this record, however, is obtained by two standard pair-mode norms and direct use of the known Boolean degree-one classification; the cluster restriction only deletes the star and identifies regularity with equal class sizes. There is no remaining unknown invariant or further structural case requiring a new argument, and no distinct extension is supplied to repair the record.
residual_risks: This value assessment does not apply to other permutation statistics, higher-order motif counts or asymptotic fluctuation results not established here.
